reason: E2 directly supports the role of edge dislocations in strength and high-T retention, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence linking configurational entropy to elastic anisotropy, nor that tuning anisotropy alters edge mobility or thermoelastic behavior. The key mechanistic premises thus lack specific prior support.
premises: Edge dislocations control yield strength in some BCC HEAs and can convey high-temperature strength retention
Elastic anisotropy in RHEAs can be tuned by composition and modulates edge dislocation mobility
High configurational entropy in RHEAs leads to elastic anisotropy that affects dislocation behavior
Reduced edge dislocation mobility at high temperature maintains yield strength and modifies thermoelastic response
Neutron diffraction line broadening can quantify edge dislocation density and character
